title: Mamata's Trinamool accuses rebel camp and Birbhum police of forging affidavits for poll panel
dek: A complaint filed at Kalighat names Ritabrata Banerjee, Arup Roy and two Nanoor police officers. The CPI(M) says it is wary of unity talks with Mamata Banerjee.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Mamata Banerjee's faction of the Trinamool Congress has filed a police complaint in Kolkata accusing the rival Democratic Trinamool Congress of forging affidavits it submitted to the Election Commission of India in the fight over the party's name and symbol, and naming two officers of a Birbhum police station among those it says took part.

The complaint was lodged at Kalighat police station by the treasurer of the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, according to reports. It names Ritabrata Banerjee, the Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly who leads the breakaway group, and the MLA Arup Roy, whom the rebels describe as the party's chairperson. It also names Sanjoy Sarkar, officer-in-charge of Nanoor police station, sub-inspector Golok Ghosh, and other unnamed officers and civic volunteers of the same station.

## What the complaint alleges

The complaint alleges a criminal conspiracy to fabricate affidavits, forge the signatures of citizens and of a notary, and misuse notarial seals, and to create other false documents for use before the Election Commission. It says affidavits were made in the names of people who never signed them or authorised anyone to do so, and that "an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station", according to reports. The treasurer said the rebels' documents had been certified by a "fake notary" and that he had evidence to support the claim.

The allegations have not been tested in any court. No response from the Democratic Trinamool Congress, from the officers named or from the police had been reported by Sunday evening, and it was not known whether a case had been registered.

## Background

The Trinamool Congress split after it lost the Assembly election in May to the BJP, ending 15 years in power, and Suvendu Adhikari became chief minister. In September the Election Commission gave the two sides temporary identities while it decides who owns the original name, All India Trinamool Congress, and its twin-flower symbol: Mamata Banerjee's group became the "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" and the rebels the "Democratic Trinamool Congress".

Both sides have sent the Commission truckloads of signed statements. The rebels said they filed six truckloads on 5 November, with signatures of more than 12 lakh workers and supporters. Mamata Banerjee's faction sent three on 15 November, including affidavits from 17 MPs, and its MP Kalyan Banerjee said then that some of the rival documents carried forged signatures. Earlier this month the faction's general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, wrote to the Commission asking it to protect his side's documents, alleging that people had attacked his Kalighat home on the night of 6 to 7 November.

Separately, the faction has asked the Speaker to disqualify 10 rebel MLAs, including Ritabrata Banerjee, under the anti-defection law; the Supreme Court has sent that dispute to the Calcutta High Court.

## Left wary of opposition unity

The complaint comes as Mamata Banerjee's camp reaches out to other opposition parties. After the Trinamool leader Kunal Ghosh called for opposition unity and Ms Banerjee met the CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby in Delhi, the party's senior Bengal leader Md Salim struck a cautious note on Sunday.

"There is nothing wrong with talking to anyone. But one should know their friends and enemies," Mr Salim told reporters in Kolkata, at an event in memory of the late CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury. He said strategy was built gradually and accused the BJP government of continuing the corruption that Trinamool had been accused of. Mr Baby said the party's approach in each state "depends on the concrete political situation existing in different states", according to reports. The organisers said the event had moved to a city hall after authorities cancelled its booking at the Eastern Zonal Cultural Centre, which Mr Salim called an attack on democratic rights.

The BJP's state president, Samik Bhattacharya, mocked the idea of a Trinamool-Left alliance, and Mr Ghosh replied that Mr Bhattacharya was in no position to say whether Ms Banerjee needed anyone's support, reports said.

## What happens next

The Election Commission is expected to examine both sets of documents before it holds hearings at which each side can challenge the other's claims. No hearing date has been announced. Kolkata's municipal elections, which would be the first major test of the two factions since the split, are on hold after the Calcutta High Court stayed the notification over ward boundaries.
